clue.text: Transferred between banks

parts.note: banks suggests money moved between financial institutions, but these are river banks and the moving is done by boat

explanation.surface: Money was moved from one bank account to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banks' tempts you to think of finance; the banks here are the two sides of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Carrying people or goods across a river by boat from one shore to the other is exactly what a ferry does.

clue.text: Work out in person

definitions.meaning: a ... is an individual, as in 'a public ...'

explanation.surface: Exercise in person rather than online.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure a sum is to calculate it, and a well-known individual is called a public figure.

clue.text: To live in the future's ideal

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone aspires to live in an ideal future.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across futuRES IDEal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside somewhere is to have your home there, a formal synonym for dwelling.

clue.text: A rendition becoming excessive

indicators.note: becoming means the letters of the phrase turn into something else, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A performance of a song that goes on far too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate means beyond reasonable limits, a direct synonym for too much.

clue.text: Give a name to first-class city of Arabia

parts.note: to dub someone is to give them a name or title
A1 is a classic phrase for first-class, written AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: Someone christens a top-quality Arabian city.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubai is a major city in the United Arab Emirates on the Arabian Peninsula.

clue.text: Sailor held by a devout Buddhist state

indicators.note: held by means the sailor is gripped inside the phrase about the Buddhist

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk or teacher
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a common abbreviation for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor is taken in by a pious Buddhist monk.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabama is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Deep South.

clue.text: Michael, the chief financial backer?

parts.note: arch- as a prefix means chief, as in archbishop
an angel is an investor who funds a theatrical show or a start-up

explanation.surface: Who is Michael, the main investor in the venture?
explanation.walkthrough: Michael is the archangel of Christian tradition; the surface makes him sound like a businessman.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael is named in the Bible as an archangel, a chief angel, so the name is an example of one.

clue.text: A bygone city with a distinctive air

parts.note: Ur was an ancient Sumerian city in Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city

explanation.surface: An ancient city with a special atmosphere about it.
explanation.definitionFit: An aura is the special atmosphere or quality that seems to surround a person or place.

clue.text: Pretended to be deeply moved

definitions.meaning: ... as in feigned or put on, like an ... accent

explanation.surface: Someone faked being emotionally stirred.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both feigned or put on and emotionally touched, two unrelated senses of one spelling.

clue.text: Complaints when sent mail goes astray

indicators.note: goes astray means the letters wander out of their places and end up rearranged

explanation.surface: People grumble when post they sent is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints in the medical sense are illnesses or disorders, as in 'a stomach complaint'.

clue.text: Gout's disrupted zest for life

indicators.note: disrupted means the letters are thrown into disorder and rearranged

parts.note: the word gout with its possessive S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A painful illness spoils someone's enjoyment of living.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Gout's is used as a letter S, giving five letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Gusto means enthusiastic enjoyment, a synonym for relish or zest.

clue.text: Call to mind

parts.note: looks like the idiom for remembering, but means a shouted warning telling someone to mind out

explanation.surface: Recall something from memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call to mind' normally means remember; here it is a call, a shout, telling someone to mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A warning shout urging caution is exactly what 'Mind!' means as an imperative.

clue.text: One all a-flutter for Real Madrid running around

indicators.note: running around means the letters chase about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is excited about the Spanish football club Real Madrid racing about the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Real Madrid is a famous Spanish football club; a red admiral is a butterfly, hence 'a-flutter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A red admiral is a common butterfly, so it is something that flutters its wings.

clue.text: Bill born with spots on the face

parts.note: AC, short for account, is a bill
née, used before a maiden name, means born; written NE

explanation.surface: A man named Bill was born with a spotty complexion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a name but is an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: The skin condition causes pimples, mostly on the face, especially in teenagers.

clue.text: Equip old fellow with weapons for the final battle

parts.note: to arm someone is to equip them with weapons
aged means old
a don is a university fellow or lecturer

explanation.surface: Give an elderly man weapons for the last great fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Equip ... with weapons' together means ARM; 'with weapons' completes that sense around 'old fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Revelation, Armageddon is the site of the last great conflict at the end of the world.

clue.text: Item of clothing that's never worn out

definitions.text: Item of clothing that's never worn out

parts.words: Item of clothing that's never worn out
parts.note: worn out suggests threadbare, but means worn on the outside, in public view

explanation.surface: A garment that lasts for ever without fraying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' reads as threadbare; it means worn on the outside, which underwear never is.
explanation.definitionFit: Underwear goes beneath other clothes, so it is never on show outside them.

clue.text: Leader of opinion?

parts.note: suggests a person who sways views, but a newspaper leader is its main opinion column

explanation.surface: Who is the person shaping public views?
explanation.walkthrough: In British newspapers a 'leader' is the editor's opinion piece, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper leader is the article giving the paper's own view, written by or for its editor.

clue.text: Reckon tea-time's changed

indicators.note: changed means the letters are altered into a different order

parts.note: the word tea-time with its possessive S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: Someone thinks the hour for afternoon tea has been moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To estimate is to judge roughly, the same as reckoning or guessing.

clue.text: Not rare words of praise

definitions.meaning: of steak, cooked right through rather than left bloody
a congratulation, as said to someone who has succeeded

explanation.surface: Words of praise that are hardly unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' looks like 'uncommon' but is the steak sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak cooked all the way through is described this way, and the same phrase congratulates someone.

clue.text: Tender bill for plant?

parts.note: sweet as in gentle and loving, like tender
Bill is a familiar short form of the name William

explanation.surface: A small invoice for a plant at the garden centre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like an invoice; it is the pet name for William.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet william is a garden flower of the pink family, so it is an example of a plant.

clue.text: Something to eat from the hand

definitions.text: Something to eat from the hand

parts.words: Something to eat from the hand
parts.note: suggests finger food, but a hand is the name for a bunch of this fruit

explanation.surface: Food you can eat with your fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'hand' is a cluster of these fruits growing together.
explanation.definitionFit: This fruit grows in bunches called hands, so one is taken from a hand and eaten.

clue.text: Strict clergyman turns up in diocese

indicators.note: in signals that the clergyman's letters are placed within the diocese

parts.note: a see is a bishop's diocese

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, stands for a clergyman

explanation.surface: A stern vicar arrives in the diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' looks like 'arrives', but signals REV read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe means harsh or rigorous, the same as strict.

clue.text: I had the French loaf

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I had
le is the French word for the

explanation.surface: Someone ate a French loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loaf' looks like bread; it is the verb meaning laze about.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to laze around doing nothing, and to idle means the same.

clue.text: Delayed action with stand-in starting film scene?

indicators.note: starting means the stand-in comes first, before the film scene

parts.note: a double is a stand-in for an actor in risky scenes
a take is one filmed version of a scene

explanation.surface: A film scene that begins with a stunt performer, shot after a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A double take is a delayed reaction, a second look when something registers late.

clue.text: Prohibition, most of all, is boring

parts.note: a ban is a prohibition

indicators.note: most of means the word loses its final letter, keeping nearly all of it

explanation.surface: Banning everything makes for dullness.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, so dull or tedious.

clue.text: I hurried round in the wet

indicators.note: round means the word for hurried goes around the letter I

parts.note: ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Someone dashed about in the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: The wet is a British colloquial name for rainy weather, as in 'out in the wet'.

clue.text: Commercial address demonstrates high esteem

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
an oration is a formal speech or address

explanation.surface: A speech in a television advert shows great respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep love and respect, so very high regard.

clue.text: Sailor died a dissolute man

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies
a rake is a man of loose, immoral habits

explanation.surface: A seaman died a debauched man.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Francis Drake was the Elizabethan English navigator who sailed around the world.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was a famous Elizabethan seafarer and naval commander, an example of a sailor.

clue.text: There's no end of such things

definitions.text: There's no end of such things

parts.words: There's no end of such things
parts.note: looks like a remark about abundance, but literally describes things without an end

explanation.surface: There are endless numbers of these things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end of' usually means plenty; here it means lacking an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no end in time, which is exactly what the clue literally says.

clue.text: The strain from row taking a long time

parts.note: a line is a row
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Tension that comes from an argument dragging on for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' and 'row' suggest stress and an argument; strain is ancestry and a row is a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain in the sense of breed or stock is a line of descent, an ancestry.
